      labels:
        app: menu-service
        version: blue
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v1.9.3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── GREEN · next ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-green-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Two full copies?
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      version: green
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        version: green
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── ACTIVE · the Service users hit ──
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-active-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ② Who gets live traffic?
  selector:
    app: menu-service
    version: blue                        # flip to green = the cutover; flip back = rollback
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---

metadata:
  name: menu-preview-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ③ How do I test green first?
  selector:
    app: menu-service
    version: green
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080

        Memory footprint

        Limits — 3 GB/pod (cap)

        The 2× bill: 8 GB reserved and 24 GB of limits for the whole overlap. See 1.4 for Blue/Green vs Recreate.

        4.1 · 4. Blue / Green

        Manual and scripted cutover

        In one sentence

        A script deploys green, smoke-tests it through the preview Service, flips the active selector, soaks, and only then scales blue to zero.

        cutover.shbash cutover.sh
        #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
NS=jahez-prod
# ── 1) deploy green and wait until every Pod is Ready ──
kubectl -n $NS apply -f menu-blue-green.yaml
kubectl -n $NS rollout status deploy/menu-green-deployment --timeout=180s
# ── 2) smoke-test green through the preview Service (no users yet) ──
kubectl -n $NS run smoke-pod --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- \
  curl -fsS http://menu-preview-service/ready || { echo "green failed smoke"; exit 1; }
# ── 3) the cutover: flip the active Service selector (atomic) ──
kubectl -n $NS patch svc menu-active-service --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"menu-service","version":"green"}}}'
# ── 4) soak; blue stays up for instant rollback ──
sleep 300
# ── 5) retire blue ──
kubectl -n $NS scale deploy/menu-blue-deployment --replicas=0
# ROLLBACK any time before step 5:
# kubectl -n $NS patch svc menu-active-service --type merge -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"blue"}}}'
        ⌘ Commands for this file
        bash cutover.sh

        run the whole cutover end to end

        💡 Command hint
        run the command

        Run the command.

          kubectl -n jahez-prod get svc menu-active-service -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'

          which colour is live now

          💡 Command hint
          read from cluster→cluster unchanged

          Read from cluster then cluster unchanged.

          • -n — namespace
          • jahez-prod — the production namespace
          • -o — output format
          Result Users are on green; blue stays scaled until step 5, so rollback is one patch away.
          ✕ When it fails The smoke test fails → the script exits before the flip; users never saw green.
          4.2 · 4. Blue / Green

          GitOps with Argo CD

          In one sentence

          The selector lives in git; the cutover is a one-line commit that Argo CD syncs, and a revert is the rollback.

          ① The logic, read first
          Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
          ① Where is the desired state?source.repoURL · paththe recipe book
          ② Where does it go?destinationthe kitchen
          ③ How is it kept in sync?syncPolicy.automateda chef who re-reads the book
          ② Full YAML
          menu-blue-green-application.yamlkubectl apply -f
          # Argo CD watches the repo folder; the cutover is a one-line commit to menu-blue-green.yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: menu-blue-green-application
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  # ① Where is the desired state?
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/jahez/menu-service.git
    targetRevision: main
    path: deploy/03-blue-green
  # ② Where does it go?
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: jahez-prod
  # ③ How is it kept in sync?
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true# a manual kubectl patch is reverted to git

            4.3 · 4. Blue / Green

            Argo Rollouts blueGreen

            In one sentence

            A Rollout object replaces the Deployment; Argo creates both ReplicaSets, points the preview Service at the new one, runs analysis, then repoints the active Service.

            ① The logic, read first
            Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
            ① What to run?replicas · templatesame as a Deployment
            ② Which Services does Argo repoint?activeService · previewServicethe two signs
            ③ Who decides the flip?autoPromotionEnabled · pre/postPromotionAnalysisthe inspector
            ④ How long is going back instant?scaleDownDelaySecondshow long blue stays warm
            Argo Rollouts blueGreen — controller-driven promotion4 steps
            1

            Deploy new ReplicaSet

            Apply the Rollout with a new image. The controller spins up the green (v2) ReplicaSet at full size; the activeService still points at blue (v1).

            ‹ Back1 / 4
            2

            prePromotionAnalysis on preview

            Green is reachable only via previewService. The controller runs the smoke AnalysisTemplate against it — no user traffic yet. Fail here and it never promotes.

            2 / 4
            3

            promote → activeService flips

            On promote (or auto if enabled), the controller repoints activeService to green. Atomic, zero-downtime. Blue stays up for scaleDownDelaySeconds.

            3 / 4
            4

            postPromotionAnalysis → scale down

            postPromotionAnalysis watches the live green; if it breaches, the controller auto-aborts back to blue. After the delay, blue is scaled to 0.

            4 / 4Done ✓
            ② Full YAML
            menu-rollout-blue-green.yamlkubectl apply -f
            apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout                            # replaces the Deployment object
metadata:
  name: menu-rollout
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What to run?
  replicas: 4
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
  strategy:
    blueGreen:
      # ② Which Services does Argo repoint?
      activeService: menu-active-service       # users
      previewService: menu-preview-service     # QA, before promotion
      # ③ Who decides the flip?
      autoPromotionEnabled: false# wait for kubectl argo rollouts promote
      prePromotionAnalysis:                    # must pass BEFORE the flip
        templates:
          - templateName: smoke-analysis-template
        args:
          - name: service-name
            value: menu-preview-service
      postPromotionAnalysis:                   # watched AFTER the flip; fail = auto-abort
        templates:
          - templateName: success-rate-analysis-template
      # ④ How long is going back instant?
      scaleDownDelaySeconds: 300# old ReplicaSet kept 5 min
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-active-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  selector:
    app: menu-service                    # Argo adds rollouts-pod-template-hash
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-preview-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  selector:
    app: menu-service
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080

            4.4 · 4. Blue / Green

            Methods compared

            In one sentence

            The objects are the same in all three methods: two ReplicaSets and an active and preview Service; only who flips the selector changes.

            MethodHow the flip happensGateRollbackBest for
            Manual / scriptedkubectl patch svca human reads dashboardspatch backsmall teams, rare releases
            GitOpscommit the selector; Argo CD syncsPR review + CIrevert the commitauditable shops

            5.0 · 5. Canary

            How Canary works

            In one sentence

            Release v2 to a small slice of traffic first, watch its metrics, and widen the slice only while it stays healthy.

            Standard definition

            A deployment strategy in which the new version is released to a small subset of traffic first and widened progressively only after it is observed to be healthy, limiting the blast radius of a bad release.

            ① The logic, read first
            Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
            ① Two tracks?stable + canary Deployments · track labelold menu and a test kitchen
            ② How is traffic split?replica ratio (5.1) or Istio weights (5.2)how many tables each kitchen serves
            ③ When do we advance?bake time + analysis (5.4–5.6)tasting before the next table
            ④ How do we go back?canary to 0 replicas or weight 0close the test kitchen
            Canary release — stepped 25% → 50% → 75% → 100%5 steps
            1

            0% — stable only

            4 stable (v1) pods, no canary. 100% of traffic on v1. Total replicas are held at 4 throughout, so the split is shifted by re-balancing the two Deployments — with 4 pods each step is an exact 25%.

            ‹ Back1 / 5
            2

            Step 1 — 25%

            Scale canary to 1 and stable to 3 (total still 4). One of four pods is v2, so ≈25% of requests hit the new version. Bake here: watch error rate, p99 latency and checkout success on the canary pods before advancing.

            2 / 5
            3

            Step 2 — 50%

            Stable 2 / canary 2. Half the fleet is v2. If the metrics held through the bake window, advance; if any breached threshold, scale canary back to 0 — that is the rollback.

            3 / 5
            4

            Step 3 — 75%

            Stable 1 / canary 3. Most traffic is on v2; this is the last checkpoint before full promotion. The shrinking stable set is your remaining safety margin.

            4 / 5
            5

            Step 4 — 100%

            Stable 0 / canary 4. Fully promoted — v2 is now the stable version (relabel it and the next release starts from here). A bad metric at any step would have scaled canary to 0 for an instant rollback.

            5 / 5Done ✓
            ② Full YAML
            menu-canary.yamlkubectl apply -f
            # Replica-ratio canary: 3 stable + 1 canary = 25% of requests on v2
# ── STABLE ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-stable-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Two tracks?
  replicas: 3# 3 of 4 = 75%
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      track: stable
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        track: stable
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v1.9.3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── CANARY ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-canary-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Two tracks?
  replicas: 1# 1 of 4 = 25%: raise to widen
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      track: canary
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        track: canary
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── SHARED SERVICE ──
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ② How is traffic split?
  selector:
    app: menu-service                    # no track key: load-balances over all 4 Pods
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080

            5.1 · 5. Canary

            Replica ratio (constant total)

            In one sentence

            Hold the total at 4 Pods and shift the split by scaling both Deployments; no extra capacity, but the warm fallback shrinks as you advance.

            Approach A — replica-ratio, constant total (4 pods)4 steps
            1

            0% — stable only

            4 v1, total 4.

            ‹ Back1 / 4
            2

            25% — stable 3 / canary 1

            Total still 4 — a stable pod was terminated to make room for the canary. Fallback capacity is now 3.

            2 / 4
            3

            50% — stable 2 / canary 2

            Two more stable pods retired. Only 2 stable left if you need to roll back.

            3 / 4
            4

            100% — canary 4

            Stable fully drained. Total stayed 4 the whole time — zero extra capacity, but no warm fallback remained near the end.

            4 / 4Done ✓
            Limits — 3 GB/pod (cap)
            Requests — 1 GB/pod (reserved)
            Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod (actual)

            Flat 4 GB reserved the whole way.

            canary-replica-ratio.shbash
            #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
NS=jahez-prod
step(){ # $1 = canary replicas, $2 = stable replicas (total stays 4)
  kubectl -n $NS scale deploy/menu-canary-deployment --replicas=$1
  kubectl -n $NS scale deploy/menu-stable-deployment --replicas=$2
  echo "canary ~$(( $1 * 100 / ($1 + $2) ))% -- baking"; }
step 1 3; sleep 600     # 25%: check error rate, p99, checkout success
step 2 2; sleep 600     # 50%
step 3 1; sleep 600     # 75%
step 4 0                # 100%: canary is the new stable
# ROLLBACK at any step:
# kubectl -n $NS scale deploy/menu-canary-deployment --replicas=0
# kubectl -n $NS scale deploy/menu-stable-deployment --replicas=4

              In one sentence

              Keep stable at full size, add the canary beside it and let an Istio VirtualService set the exact share, independent of Pod count.

              Approach B — additive / traffic-routed (stable kept at full)5 steps

              4 v1, total 4. Traffic 100% stable.

              2

kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: menu-destination-rule
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  host: menu-service
  # ① Which Pods form each subset?
  subsets:
    - name: stable

    - name: canary

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: menu-virtual-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  hosts:
    - menu-service
  http:
    - name: primary
      # ② What share does each subset get?
      route:
        - destination:
            host: menu-service
            subset: stable
          weight: 75# patch these two weights to move traffic
        - destination:
            host: menu-service
            subset: canary
          weight: 25# exact %, independent of Pod count
              canary-weighted.shbash
              #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
NS=jahez-prod
set_weight(){ # $1 = canary %
  kubectl -n $NS patch vs menu-virtual-service --type json -p "[
    {\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/http/0/route/0/weight\",\"value\":$((100-$1))},
    {\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/http/0/route/1/weight\",\"value\":$1}]"
  echo "canary at $1%"; }
set_weight 1;  sleep 600     # tiny exposure first
set_weight 5;  sleep 600
set_weight 25; sleep 600
set_weight 50; sleep 600
set_weight 100               # promoted; rollback = set_weight 0

                5.3 · 5. Canary

                Progression shapes

                In one sentence

                The weight curve is a design choice: equal steps, a timer, tiny-then-fast, or one step and a jump.

                Stepped / staged

                Definition

                A canary progression that advances through a fixed set of equal traffic weights (25 → 50 → 75 → 100), pausing at each for a bake window and a metric gate before the next jump.

                Principles

                • Equal weight increments, one checkpoint per step.
                • Bake + automated metric analysis at every stage.
                • Advance only on healthy signals; otherwise hold or roll back.
                • Rollback = shift weight back / scale canary to 0.

                Best practices

                • Keep the steps few and even so each is easy to reason about.
                • Gate every step on the same metric set (error rate, p99, checkout success).
                • Make the bake long enough to cover at least one real traffic cycle.
                • Automate the steps with Argo Rollouts or Flagger, not a human clicking.
                ◆ When to use

                The sensible default for most releases — when you want simple, auditable, predictable stages and moderate risk.

                Weight curve

                Canary (v2) traffic %
                Stable (v1) traffic %

                Even 25% jumps with a hold (bake) between each — the classic staircase.

                Cluster walkthrough — Stepped / staged5 steps
                1

                0% — stable only

                4 v1 serving, no canary.

                ‹ Back1 / 5
                2

                25%

                Canary added on top (stable kept warm). Router sends 25% to v2. Bake and check metrics.

                2 / 5
                3

                50%

                Half the traffic on v2; full stable fleet still standing by.

                3 / 5
                4

                75%

                Last checkpoint before full. Stable remains the fallback.

                4 / 5
                5

                100%

                All traffic on v2; stable stays warm until the soak ends, then is retired.

                5 / 5Done ✓
                Limits — 3 GB/pod
                Requests — 1 GB/pod
                Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod

                Footprint: Reserved memory climbs one step per stage to 8 GB at 100%, then drops at cutover — the largest sustained overhead of the four shapes.

                Linear

                Definition

                A canary progression that raises the weight by a fixed increment on a fixed timer (e.g. +10% every 5 min) until 100%, with automated analysis aborting on any regression.

                Principles

                • Equal increments on a clock, not on a manual gate.
                • Automated metric analysis alone decides advance vs. abort.
                • Total rollout duration is predictable from increment × interval.

                Best practices

                • Use only with trustworthy automated analysis + auto-rollback wired in.
                • Pick increment and interval so each step sees statistically enough traffic.
                • Freeze promotion automatically during an active incident or peak window.
                ◆ When to use

                Mature pipelines with solid metric gating — when predictable timing matters and the change is moderate-risk.

                Weight curve

                Canary (v2) traffic %
                Stable (v1) traffic %

                A straight diagonal: equal increments on a fixed timer, no manual pause.

                Cluster walkthrough — Linear6 steps
                1

                0%

                4 v1 serving.

                ‹ Back1 / 6
                2

                20%

                Timer ticks: +20%. Canary scaled for its share; analysis runs continuously.

                2 / 6
                3

                40%

                Another interval, another step. No human gate — the analysis would auto-abort on a bad signal.

                3 / 6
                4

                60%

                Weight keeps climbing on the clock.

                4 / 6
                5

                80%

                Nearly there; canary scaled up for capacity.

                5 / 6
                6

                100%

                Full weight reached on schedule; stable retired after soak.

                6 / 6Done ✓
                Limits — 3 GB/pod
                Requests — 1 GB/pod
                Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod

                Footprint: Same 8 GB peak as stepped, but a gradual climb and a little less time at the top. The appeal is operational simplicity and predictable timing, not cost.

                Exponential / front-loaded

                Definition

                A canary progression that starts with very small weights (1% → 2% → 5%) and accelerates (→ 25% → 50% → 100%) as confidence grows, minimising exposure during the riskiest early phase.

                Principles

                • Tiny early blast radius; most observation spent at low weight.
                • Accelerate only once the early signals are clean.
                • Weight is decoupled from pod count — needs weighted routing for sub-replica %.

                Best practices

                • Requires a mesh/ingress to express 1–5% weights (replica ratio can't).
                • Hold longest at the first 1–5% step — that's where you catch disasters.
                • Pair with anomaly detection, not just static thresholds.
                ◆ When to use

                High-risk or hard-to-reverse changes, and large user bases where even 1% is meaningful traffic.

                Weight curve

                Canary (v2) traffic %
                Stable (v1) traffic %

                Flat and low early (1–5%), then it accelerates — minimal early exposure.

                Cluster walkthrough — Exponential / front-loaded5 steps
                1

                0%

                4 v1 serving.

                ‹ Back1 / 5
                2

                1%

                One canary pod, router sends just 1% — almost nobody is exposed. Hold here longest.

                2 / 5
                3

                5%

                Still one canary pod; weight nudged up as early metrics stay clean.

                3 / 5
                4

                25%

                Confidence rising — accelerate, scale canary for capacity.

                4 / 5
                5

                100%

                Final leap to full once metrics are trusted; stable retired after soak.

                5 / 5Done ✓
                Limits — 3 GB/pod
                Requests — 1 GB/pod
                Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod

                Footprint: Sits low (≈5 GB, one canary pod) for most of the rollout and only spikes to 8 GB at the very end — the smallest area-under-curve, so the most resource-efficient way to be cautious.

                Single-step

                Definition

                A canary progression with one intermediate weight (e.g. 25%) held for a bake, then a direct jump to 100%.

                Principles

                • One checkpoint, then full cutover — the fewest stages.
                • Fastest of the staged shapes.
                • All the risk rides on that single jump from 25% to 100%.

                Best practices

                • Use only for low-risk changes or behind strong automated gates.
                • Keep the single bake long enough to be statistically meaningful.
                • Make sure instant rollback is wired before the jump.
                ◆ When to use

                Low-risk config or bugfix releases — when speed matters more than granular validation.

                Weight curve

                Canary (v2) traffic %
                Stable (v1) traffic %

                One hold at 25%, then a single vertical leap straight to 100%.

                Cluster walkthrough — Single-step3 steps
                1

                0%

                4 v1 serving.

                ‹ Back1 / 3
                2

                25% (bake)

                One canary stage. Hold and watch metrics — this is the only checkpoint.

                2 / 3
                3

                100%

                Jump straight to full. Nobody validated 50% or 75%, so a latent fault now hits everyone.

                3 / 3Done ✓
                Limits — 3 GB/pod
                Requests — 1 GB/pod
                Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod

                Footprint: Cheapest by area: a single 5 GB canary stage, then a brief 8 GB spike at cutover. The risk lives in the traffic curve, not the resource curve.

                ▲ Choosing a shape

                Stepped is the safe default; linear swaps manual gates for timer-driven automation; exponential is the most cautious and most resource-efficient for risky changes; single-step is fastest but validates the least. Drive any of them with Argo Rollouts or Flagger so each step is gated by automated metric analysis with auto-rollback.

                5.4 · 5. Canary

                Argo Rollouts canary

                In one sentence

                A Rollout encodes the whole progression as steps; the controller sets weights, waits, runs analysis and aborts on failure.

                ① The logic, read first
                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① What to run?templatesame as a Deployment
                ② Which Services and routes?stableService · canaryService · trafficRoutingthe levers
                ③ What is the plan?stepsthe recipe, step by step
                Argo Rollouts canary — the step machine5 steps
                1

                setWeight 25

                Controller patches the Istio VirtualService to 25% canary and scales the canary ReplicaSet. Traffic split is exact, set by the mesh.

                ‹ Back1 / 5
                2

                pause 10m + analysis

                Controller holds, then runs the AnalysisTemplate — querying Prometheus for success-rate. This is the gate.

                2 / 5
                3

                analysis pass → setWeight 50

                Metrics cleared the threshold, so the machine advances to the next step automatically.

                3 / 5
                4

                setWeight 75

                Another pause + the same checks. A failure here would abort and shift weight straight back to stable.

                4 / 5
                5

                setWeight 100 → promoted

                All steps passed; canary becomes the new stable. The whole sequence was declarative — no human in the loop unless a step failed.

                5 / 5Done ✓
                ② Full YAML
                menu-rollout-canary.yamlkubectl apply -f
                apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: menu-rollout
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What to run?
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
  strategy:
    canary:
      # ② Which Services and routes does Argo control?
      stableService: menu-stable-service
      canaryService: menu-canary-service
      trafficRouting:
        istio:
          virtualService:
            name: menu-virtual-service
            routes:
              - primary
      # ③ What is the step plan?
      steps:
        - setWeight: 25
        - pause:
            duration: 10m
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: success-rate-analysis-template
        - setWeight: 50
        - pause:
            duration: 10m
        - setWeight: 75
        - pause:
            duration: 10m
        - setWeight: 100

  http:

      route:
        - destination:

          weight: 100
        - destination:

          weight: 0

                5.5 · 5. Canary

                Flagger

                In one sentence

                Flagger wraps a normal Deployment and runs the whole ramp itself from one Canary resource: +stepWeight per interval, promote at maxWeight, roll back after threshold failures.

                ① The logic, read first
                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① Which workload?targetRefthe dish under test
                ② Which Services?servicegenerated plates
                ③ How does the ramp run?interval · stepWeight · maxWeight · thresholdthe auto-pilot
                ④ What counts as healthy?metricsthe taste test
                ② Full YAML
                menu-canary-flagger.yamlkubectl apply -f
                apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-service-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
apiVersion: flagger.app/v1beta1
kind: Canary
metadata:
  name: menu-service-canary
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  provider: istio
  # ① Which workload does Flagger take over?
  targetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: menu-service-deployment         # Flagger clones it to -primary
  # ② Which Services does it generate?
  service:
    name: menu-service                    # creates menu-service, -primary, -canary
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
  # ③ How does the ramp run?
  analysis:
    interval: 1m                          # one loop per minute
    threshold: 5# 5 failed checks = rollback
    maxWeight: 50# ramp up to 50% ...
    stepWeight: 10# ... in +10% steps, then promote
    # ④ What counts as healthy?
    metrics:
      - name: request-success-rate
        thresholdRange:
          min: 99# at least 99%
        interval: 1m
      - name: request-duration
        thresholdRange:
          max: 500# p99 at most 500 ms
        interval: 1m
    webhooks:
      - name: load-test
        url: http://flagger-loadtester.test/
        metadata:
          cmd: "hey -z 1m -q 10 -c 2 http://menu-service-canary.jahez-prod/"

                Flagger creates menu-service-deployment-primary and scales your Deployment to 0 between releases.

                •② serviceobjectgenerates menu-service, menu-service-primary, menu-service-canary
                •③ analysis.intervaldurationloop period
                •③ analysis.stepWeightinteger+% per passing loop
                •③ analysis.maxWeightintegerlast weight before promotion
                •③ analysis.thresholdintegerfailed checks before rollback
                •④ analysis.metricslistbuilt-in request-success-rate and request-duration, or MetricTemplates
                ④ Deep dive
                ◆ Argo Rollouts vs Flagger

                Argo Rollouts: an explicit step machine and a Rollout you promote or abort. Flagger: wraps a Deployment and automates the ramp from one CR. Both need Prometheus and, for exact weights, a mesh or ingress.

                5.6 · 5. Canary

                AnalysisTemplate

                In one sentence

                An AnalysisTemplate is a reusable metric check; Argo Rollouts runs it as an AnalysisRun and turns the result into continue, pause or abort.

                ① The logic, read first
                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① What can the caller pass in?argsblanks on the form
                ② Where does the number come from?providerthe thermometer
                ③ When is it a pass?successCondition · interval · count · failureLimitthe pass mark
                ② Full YAML
                analysis-templates.yamlkubectl apply -f
                # ── Gate 1 · smoke test the preview Service with a Job ──
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: smoke-analysis-template
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What can the caller pass in?
  args:
    - name: service-name
  metrics:
    - name: smoke
      # ③ When is it a pass?
      count: 1
      failureLimit: 0
      # ② Where does the measurement come from?
      provider:
        job:
          spec:
            backoffLimit: 0
            template:
              spec:
                restartPolicy: Never
                containers:
                  - name: smoke
                    image: curlimages/curl:8.10.1
                    args:
                      - "-fsS"
                      - "http://{{args.service-name}}/ready"
---
# ── Gate 2 · live success rate from Prometheus ──
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: success-rate-analysis-template
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  metrics:
    - name: success-rate
      # ③ When is it a pass?
      interval: 1m
      count: 5# 5 measurements
      successCondition: result[0] >= 0.99  # at least 99% non-5xx
      failureLimit: 2# 3rd failure aborts
      # ② Where does the measurement come from?
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus-service.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="menu-service",code!~"5.."}[2m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="menu-service"}[2m]))

                ④ Deep dive
                ▲ No data is not a pass

                A query that returns empty (no traffic yet on the canary) is Inconclusive. Run a load-test step first, or set inconclusiveLimit.

                6.0 · 6. A/B testing

                How A/B testing works

                In one sentence

                Route specific users, not a random share, to a variant based on a request attribute, and keep each user on the same variant so results can be measured.

                Standard definition

                A release strategy that serves two or more versions simultaneously to different user segments, chosen by request attributes such as headers, cookies, geography or device, to compare their behaviour or business outcomes. The split is deterministic per user.

                Canary asks "is v2 stable?"; A/B asks "is v2 better for this segment?". It needs L7 routing, ingress-nginx or Istio, because a Service routes at L4 and cannot read headers.

                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① Which variants run?two Deployments · variant labelmenu A and menu B
                ② How does the router reach each?one Service per varianttwo doors
                ③ Who goes where?Ingress annotations or VirtualService matchthe host at the entrance
                ④ Is it sticky?cookie or edge-set headera wristband
                MethodLooks atSticky?Who sets itingress-nginxIstioSection
                HeaderHTTP headerif the edge sets it every timeclient · edge · appcanary-by-headerheaders6.4
                Query param?key=valueper linkwhoever builds the linkconfig snippetqueryParams6.5
                PathURL pathyesthe user navigatespath ruleuri.prefix6.6
                Cookiecookie valueyesapp sets it oncecanary-by-cookiecookie regex6.7
                Weightnothing: random %nothe routercanary-weightweight6.8
                ✕ ingress-nginx or Istio, never both

                They are two L7 routers that express the same rule in different syntax. In every case below, Option 1 and Option 2 are alternatives: apply only the one your cluster runs.

                ▲ Bucket upstream

                Assign users in the app or edge and pass a stable x-jahez-beta header or cookie so a user never flips variants mid-session. Track the variant as an analytics dimension.

                Memory footprint

                Limits — 3 GB/pod (cap)
                Requests — 1 GB/pod (reserved)
                Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod (actual)

                A 6 GB plateau for the length of the experiment (days or weeks), not a short surge.

                6.1 · 6. A/B testing

                Variant Deployments and Services

                In one sentence

                Two Deployments told apart by a variant label, each behind its own Service, so a router can send a request to exactly one of them.

                ① The logic, read first
                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① Which variants run?variant: a · variant: btwo menus
                ② How does the router reach each?menu-a-service · menu-b-servicetwo doors
                ② Full YAML
                menu-ab-deployments.yamlkubectl apply -f
                # ── A · control ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-a-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which variants run?
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      variant: a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        variant: a
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v1.9.3      # current layout
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── B · experiment ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-b-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which variants run?
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      variant: b
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        variant: b
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0      # new menu layout
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-a-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ② How does the router reach each variant?
  selector:
    app: menu-service
    variant: a
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-b-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ② How does the router reach each variant?
  selector:
    app: menu-service
    variant: b
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080

                6.2 · 6. A/B testing

                The ingress-nginx canary overlay

                In one sentence

                A second Ingress for the same host and path, marked canary: "true", siphons a slice off the main Ingress and sends it to menu-b-service.

                A normal Ingress maps one host + path to one backend. ingress-nginx splits by merging a main Ingress (100% → menu-a-service) with a canary Ingress that captures the matching slice.

                AnnotationWhat the canary capturesUsed for
                canary: "true"nothing alone: enables the overlay (required)both
                canary-by-header + -valuerequests whose header equals the valueA/B
                canary-by-header-patternheader matches a regexA/B
                canary-by-cookiecookie value is alwaysA/B sticky
                canary-weighta random % of all requestscanary release
                ◆ Precedence

                One canary Ingress per main Ingress. With several conditions set, ingress-nginx evaluates header → cookie → weight; the first that applies wins.

                ③ Every property
                •nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canarystringrequired"true" marks the overlay
                •nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-headerstringheader name; value "always" → canary, "never" → main
                •nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header-valuestringexact value that selects the canary
                •nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-cookiestringcookie name; "always" / "never"
                •nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weightstring0–100 random share
                nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weight-totalstringdenominator for finer weights

                Default 100

                6.3 · 6. A/B testing

                The Istio VirtualService and Gateway

                In one sentence

                One VirtualService holds an ordered list of rules; the first rule whose match is true picks the backend, and a rule with no match is the default.

                ① The logic, read first
                Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                ① Which proxy pods receive edge traffic?Gateway.selectorthe front gate
                ② Which hosts and ports are open?Gateway.serversopening hours
                ③ Which rule wins?VirtualService.http[] ordertop to bottom
                ② Full YAML
                jahez-public-gateway.yamlkubectl apply -f
                # One edge Gateway, shared by every VirtualService that serves menu.jahez.sa
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: jahez-public-gateway
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  # ① Which proxy pods receive the traffic?
  selector:
    istio: ingressgateway
  # ② Which hosts and ports are open?
  servers:
    - port:
        number: 443
        name: https
        protocol: HTTPS
      hosts:
        - "jahez-prod/menu.jahez.sa"
      tls:
        mode: SIMPLE
        credentialName: menu-jahez-sa-tls-secret   # issued by cert-manager in istio-system

                6.4 · 6. A/B testing

                Header

                In one sentence

                Route on a header the app or edge adds, e.g. x-jahez-beta: true for opted-in beta users.

                Header routing — request flow4 steps
                1

                Two requests arrive

                One carries the attribute the rule looks for; the other does not. Both hit the router.

                ‹ Back1 / 4
                2

                Router reads the attribute

                The router inspects each request against rule 1, top of the list.

                2 / 4
                3

                Match → menu-b-service

                Request #1 matches (header = true) → routed to menu-b-service (the experiment).

                3 / 4
                4

                No match → menu-a-service

                Request #2 matches no rule → falls through to the default → menu-a-service (control).

                4 / 4Done ✓

                OPTION 1 ingress-nginx

                ab-header-nginx.yamlkubectl apply -f
                # ── Main Ingress: everyone gets menu-a-service ──
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: menu-main-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: menu.jahez.sa
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: menu-a-service
                port:
                  number: 80
---
# ── Canary Ingress: x-jahez-beta: true goes to menu-b-service ──
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: menu-b-header-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
  annotations:
    # ① Which slice does the overlay capture?
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header: "x-jahez-beta"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header-value: "true"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: menu.jahez.sa                # same host + path as the main Ingress
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: menu-b-service     # ② where the slice goes
                port:
                  number: 80

                            Cookie (sticky)

                            In one sentence

                            Bucket a user once with a cookie, then keep them on the same variant for every later request.

                            Cookie routing — request flow4 steps
                            1

                            Two requests arrive

                            One carries the attribute the rule looks for; the other does not. Both hit the router.

                            ‹ Back1 / 4
                            2

                            Router reads the attribute

                            The router inspects each request against rule 1, top of the list.

                            2 / 4
                            3

                            Match → menu-b-service

                            Request #1 matches (cookie has =v2) → routed to menu-b-service (the experiment).

                            3 / 4
                            4

                            No match → menu-a-service

                            Request #2 matches no rule → falls through to the default → menu-a-service (control).

                            4 / 4Done ✓

                            OPTION 1 ingress-nginx

                            ab-cookie-nginx.yamlkubectl apply -f
                            # ── Main Ingress: everyone gets menu-a-service ──
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: menu-main-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: menu.jahez.sa
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: menu-a-service
                port:
                  number: 80
---
# ── Canary Ingress: cookie jahez_experiment=always goes to menu-b-service ──
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: menu-b-cookie-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
  annotations:
    # ① Which slice does the overlay capture?
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-cookie: "jahez_experiment"   # value "always" = B, "never" = A
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: menu.jahez.sa                # same host + path as the main Ingress
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: menu-b-service     # ② where the slice goes
                port:
                  number: 80

kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: menu-ab-virtual-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  hosts:
    - menu.jahez.sa

                                6.8 · 6. A/B testing

                                Weight (random %)

                                In one sentence

                                Send a random share of all requests to menu-b-service; not sticky, so pair it with a cookie for a real experiment.

                                Weight routing — request flow4 steps
                                1

                                Requests arrive

                                Every request is eligible; nothing about the request is inspected.

                                ‹ Back1 / 4
                                2

                                Router rolls the dice

                                Per request, the router applies the configured weight — 20% to canary.

                                2 / 4
                                3

                                ~20% → menu-b-service

                                Roughly one in five requests is sent to menu-b-service at random.

                                3 / 4
                                4

                                ~80% → menu-a-service

                                The remaining ~80% go to menu-a-service. Not sticky — the same user can flip.

                                4 / 4Done ✓

                                OPTION 1 ingress-nginx

                                ab-weight-nginx.yamlkubectl apply -f

                                    ▲ Weights are per request

                                    The same user can land on A, then B. For product experiments, use weight only to pick the bucket once, then pin it with a cookie (6.7).

                                    7.0 · 7. Shadow / mirror

                                    How Shadow works

                                    In one sentence

                                    Send a copy of live production traffic to v2 while users keep getting answers only from v1; v2 is tested under real load with zero user risk.

                                    Standard definition

                                    A deployment strategy in which a copy of live production traffic is mirrored to the new version in parallel with the current one, while only the current version's responses are returned to users.

                                    Live path
                                    Mirrored path (discarded)
                                    Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                                    ① Which Pods are live and which shadow?DestinationRule.subsetsthe real kitchen and the test kitchen
                                    ② Who answers the user?http[].routethe waiter only takes plates from the real kitchen
                                    ③ Who gets a copy?http[].mirrora copy of every order ticket
                                    ④ How much is copied?mirrorPercentagehow many tickets get copied
                                    ✕ The side-effect trap

                                    Mirrored requests run real code. If v2 writes to orders-db, charges Mada or sends notifications, shadowing does it twice. Isolate first (7.2).

                                    Memory footprint

                                    Limits — 3 GB/pod (cap)
                                    Requests — 1 GB/pod (reserved)
                                    Usage — 0.5–1.5 GB/pod (actual)

                                    Same 8 GB as Blue/Green for the mirror window; shadow usage tracks production because it sees the same requests.

                                    7.1 · 7. Shadow / mirror

                                    Istio mirror and DestinationRule

                                    In one sentence

                                    A VirtualService routes 100% to the live subset and mirrors a copy to the shadow subset; a DestinationRule defines the two subsets by version label.

                                    ① The logic, read first

                                    The four questions of 7.0 map to four blocks in the file.

                                    ② Full YAML
                                    menu-shadow.yamlkubectl apply -f
                                    # ── v1 · answers users ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-v1-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      version: v1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        version: v1
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v1.9.3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ── v2 · shadow, answers nobody (isolated in 7.2) ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-v2-shadow-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 4# sized for 100% mirrored load
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      version: v2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        version: v2
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  selector:
    app: menu-service
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: menu-destination-rule
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  host: menu-service
  # ① Which Pods are live and which are the shadow?
  subsets:
    - name: live
      labels:
        version: v1
    - name: shadow
      labels:
        version: v2
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: menu-mirror-virtual-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  hosts:
    - menu-service
  http:
    - route:
        # ② Who answers the user?
        - destination:
            host: menu-service
            subset: live
          weight: 100
      # ③ Who gets a copy?
      mirror:
        host: menu-service
        subset: shadow
      # ④ How much is copied?
      mirrorPercentage:
        value: 100.0# start at 10.0 in production
                                    ⌘ Commands for this file
                                    kubectl -n jahez-prod apply -f menu-shadow.yaml

                                    start mirroring

                                    see shadow requests (Host ends in -shadow)

                                    💡 Command hint

                                    Read from cluster then cluster unchanged.

                                    • -n — namespace

                                    • -l — label selector: only objects with this label

                                    stop mirroring

                                    💡 Command hint

                                    Change route weights then Istio reprograms proxies then traffic moves.

                                    • -n — namespace

                                    • --type — patch type: merge, json or strategic
                                    • -p — the patch body (JSON or YAML)
                                    ③ Every property
                                    ③ Every property
                                    •① DestinationRule.subsetslistrequiredlive = version v1, shadow = version v2
                                    •② route[].destinationobjectthe only answer returned to users
                                    ③ mirror.host · mirror.subsetobjectwhere copies go; fire-and-forget

                                    The proxy appends -shadow to the Host header of mirrored requests, so v2 logs can tell them apart.

                                    ④ mirrorPercentage.valuedoubleshare copied
                                    ValueMeaning
                                    10.0safe first step
                                    100.0full load test

                                    Default 100 when mirror is set

                                    7.2 · 7. Shadow / mirror

                                    Isolating side effects

                                    In one sentence

                                    Point every side effect of the shadow at a sandbox, then block its egress to production so a mistake cannot double-charge a customer.

                                    ① The logic, read first
                                    Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
                                    ① Which database?ORDERS_DB_HOSTa practice kitchen
                                    ② Which payment keys?mada-sandbox-secretplay money
                                    ③ Where do notifications go?NOTIFY_URLa muted phone
                                    ④ What if the app ignores config?NetworkPolicy egressa locked door
                                    ② Full YAML
                                    menu-shadow-isolation.yamlkubectl apply -f
                                    # The shadow must never write to production. Point every side effect at a sandbox.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: menu-shadow-config-map
  namespace: jahez-prod
data:
  # ① Which database?
  ORDERS_DB_HOST: "orders-shadow-db-rw.jahez-shadow.svc"    # restored nightly copy
  # ③ Where do notifications go?
  NOTIFY_URL: "http://notification-sink-service.jahez-shadow.svc/discard"
  SHADOW_MODE: "true"                                       # app skips outbound webhooks
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: mada-sandbox-secret
  namespace: jahez-prod
type: Opaque
stringData:
  # ② Which payment keys?
  MADA_API_KEY: "sandbox-key-replace-me"                    # never the live key
  MADA_BASE_URL: "https://sandbox.mada.example/api"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-v2-shadow-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      version: v2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-service
        version: v2
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: menu-shadow-config-map
            - secretRef:
                name: mada-sandbox-secret
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
---
# ④ What if the app ignores the config? Block egress to production anyway.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: menu-shadow-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-service
      version: v2
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:                                # only the shadow namespace
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: jahez-shadow
    - to:                                # and DNS
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
      ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
                                    ⌘ Commands for this file
                                    kubectl -n jahez-prod apply -f menu-shadow-isolation.yaml

                                    isolate the shadow

                                    💡 Command hint

                                    Read the file then send to API server then create or update objects.

                                    • -n — namespace
                                    • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                    • -f — file to read
                                    • menu-shadow-isolation.yaml — manifest file or folder
                                    kubectl -n jahez-prod exec deploy/menu-v2-shadow-deployment -- nc -zv orders-db-rw.jahez-prod.svc 5432

                                    must time out: egress blocked

                                    run the command

                                    Run the command.

                                    • -n — namespace
                                    • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                    • deploy/menu-v2-shadow-deployment — the Deployment named menu-v2-shadow-deployment
                                    ③ Every property
                                    ③ Every property
                                    •① ORDERS_DB_HOSTstringa restored copy in jahez-shadow, never orders-db-rw
                                    •② mada-sandbox-secretSecretsandbox keys; the live key must not exist in the shadow Pod
                                    •③ NOTIFY_URLstringa sink that discards push, SMS and email
                                    ④ menu-shadow-network-policyNetworkPolicyegress only to jahez-shadow and DNS

                                    Defence in depth: if the app ignores its config, packets to production are dropped. Needs a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy.

service/menu-service unchanged

                                      ✕ When it fails The Deployment "menu-service-deployment" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: … field is immutable → you changed the selector; delete and recreate.

                                      [--dry-run=server] [--server-side] [-R]

                                      ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample

                                      deploy/02-rolling-update/                                      		kubectl apply -f menu-service-deployment.yaml -n jahez-prod

                                      client                                      		kubectl apply -f menu-service-deployment.yaml --dry-run=server -n jahez-prod
                                      --server-sideserver-side apply with field ownershiptruekubectl apply -f menu-service-deployment.yaml --server-side -n jahez-prod
                                      -Rrecurse into sub-folderstruekubectl apply -R -f deploy/05-ab-testing/ -n jahez-prod

                                      jahez-lab                                      		kubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod
                                      Watch out

                                      Control a rollout

                                      In one sentence

                                      Pause, resume, undo and scale: the levers that change a rollout already in flight.

                                      kubectl rollout pause · resume

kubectl set env deploy/menu-service-deployment MENU_LAYOUT=grid -n jahez-prod

                                      8.4 · 8. Commands

                                      Switch traffic

                                      In one sentence

                                      Blue/Green, ratio canary and A/B move traffic by changing routing objects, not Pods.

kubectl patch svc menu-active-service --type merge -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"menu-service","version":"green"}}}' -n jahez-prod
kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=menu-active-service -n jahez-prod

                                      kubectl patch vs

                                      Change Istio route weights: move a weighted canary or A/B split.

                                      kubectl patch vs menu-virtual-service --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/1/weight","value":50},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/0/weight","value":50}]' -n jahez-prod
                                      💡 Command hint
                                      change route weights→Istio reprograms proxies→traffic moves

                                      Change route weights then Istio reprograms proxies then traffic moves.

                                      • --type — patch type: merge, json or strategic
                                      • -p — the patch body (JSON or YAML)
                                      • -n — namespace
                                      • jahez-prod — the production namespace

                                      ✕ When it fails Weights not summing to 100 are rejected by Istio validation.

                                      8.5 · 8. Commands

                                      Argo Rollouts plugin

                                      In one sentence

                                      The kubectl-argo-rollouts plugin drives a Rollout: watch it, skip a pause, abort, retry or undo.

                                      kubectl argo rollouts get rollout

                                      Live tree of the Rollout: steps, weights, ReplicaSets, AnalysisRuns.

                                      kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod --watch
                                      💡 Command hint
                                      read the Rollout→cluster unchanged

                                      Read the Rollout then cluster unchanged.

                                      • -n — namespace
                                      • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                      • --watch — keep watching for changes
                                      Output · example output
                                      Name:            menu-rollout
Status:          ॥ Paused
Strategy:        Canary
  Step:          2/8
  SetWeight:     25
  ActualWeight:  25
Images:          ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v2.4.0 (canary)
                 ghcr.io/jahez/menu-service:v1.9.3 (stable)
                                      Result You see the current step and both images.
                                      ✕ When it fails Needs the kubectl-argo-rollouts plugin installed on your machine.
                                      Template
                                      kubectl argo rollouts get rollout <ROLLOUT> [-n <NAMESPACE>] [flags]
                                      Parameters
                                      ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample
                                      <ROLLOUT> requiredRollout namemenu-rolloutkubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod --watch
                                      --watchrefresh live—kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout --watch -n jahez-prod
                                      -n, --namespacenamespace of the objectjahez-prod
                                      jahez-lab                                      		kubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod
                                      Watch out
                                      • Status ✖ Degraded means an analysis failed and the Rollout aborted.
                                      Examples · by flag, one each
                                      FlagFull commandWhat it shows
                                      <ROLLOUT>kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod --watchRollout name
                                      --watchkubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout --watch -n jahez-prodrefresh live
                                      -n, --namespacekubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prodnamespace of the object
                                      Examples · by task
                                      tasks.shbash
                                      # ── Task: watch a canary in a second terminal ──
kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout --watch -n jahez-prod

                                      kubectl argo rollouts promote

                                      Skip the current pause (or with --full, every remaining step).

                                      kubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      💡 Command hint
                                      skip the current pause→next step runs

                                      Skip the current pause then next step runs.

                                      • -n — namespace
                                      • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                      Output · example output
                                      rollout 'menu-rollout' promoted
                                      Result The next setWeight runs now.
                                      ✕ When it fails Promoting a Rollout that is not paused does nothing.
                                      Template
                                      kubectl argo rollouts promote <ROLLOUT> [-n <NAMESPACE>] [flags]
                                      Parameters
                                      ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample
                                      <ROLLOUT> requiredRollout namemenu-rolloutkubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      --fullskip every remaining step and analysis—kubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout --full -n jahez-prod
                                      -n, --namespacenamespace of the objectjahez-prod
                                      jahez-lab                                      		kubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod
                                      Watch out
                                      • --full also skips analysis: use it only in an emergency fix-forward.
                                      Examples · by flag, one each
                                      FlagFull commandWhat it shows
                                      <ROLLOUT>kubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout -n jahez-prodRollout name
                                      --fullkubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout --full -n jahez-prodskip every remaining step and analysis
                                      -n, --namespacekubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prodnamespace of the object
                                      Examples · by task
                                      tasks.shbash

kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
kubectl argo rollouts promote menu-rollout -n jahez-prod

                                      kubectl argo rollouts abort · retry

                                      Stop a rollout and send all traffic back to stable; retry clears the abort.

                                      kubectl argo rollouts abort menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      💡 Command hint
                                      stop the rollout→traffic back to stable

                                      Stop the rollout then traffic back to stable.

                                      • -n — namespace
                                      • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                      Output · example output
                                      rollout 'menu-rollout' aborted
                                      Result Weight 0, canary scaled down; status Degraded until you retry or change the image.
                                      ✕ When it fails Aborting does not revert the template: run undo or set image to the old tag to become Healthy.
                                      Template
                                      kubectl argo rollouts abort · retry <ROLLOUT> [-n <NAMESPACE>] [flags]
                                      Parameters
                                      ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample
                                      <ROLLOUT> requiredRollout namemenu-rolloutkubectl argo rollouts abort menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      -n, --namespacenamespace of the objectjahez-prod
                                      jahez-lab                                      		kubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod
                                      Watch out
                                      • After abort, retry starts the same steps again with the same image.
                                      Examples · by flag, one each
                                      FlagFull commandWhat it shows
                                      <ROLLOUT>kubectl argo rollouts abort menu-rollout -n jahez-prodRollout name
                                      -n, --namespacekubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prodnamespace of the object
                                      Examples · by task
                                      tasks.shbash
                                      # ── Task: abort, investigate, retry ──
kubectl argo rollouts abort menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
kubectl get analysisruns -n jahez-prod
kubectl argo rollouts retry rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod

                                      kubectl argo rollouts undo

                                      Roll the Rollout back to a previous revision, through its strategy.

                                      kubectl argo rollouts undo menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      💡 Command hint
                                      pick an old revision→new rollout starts

                                      Pick an old revision then new rollout starts.

                                      • -n — namespace
                                      • jahez-prod — the production namespace
                                      Output · example output
                                      rollout 'menu-rollout' undo
                                      Result The old template becomes a new revision and goes through the steps.
                                      ✕ When it fails The old ReplicaSet may already be scaled down; undo then needs fresh Pods.
                                      Template
                                      kubectl argo rollouts undo <ROLLOUT> [-n <NAMESPACE>] [flags]

                                      ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample

                                      --to-revisiontarget revision3kubectl argo rollouts undo menu-rollout --to-revision=3 -n jahez-prod
                                      -n, --namespacenamespace of the objectjahez-prod
                                      jahez-lab                                      		kubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod
                                      Watch out
                                      • Blue/Green undo within scaleDownDelaySeconds is instant: the old Pods still run.
                                      Examples · by flag, one each
                                      FlagFull commandWhat it shows
                                      <ROLLOUT>kubectl argo rollouts undo menu-rollout -n jahez-prodRollout name
                                      --to-revisionkubectl argo rollouts undo menu-rollout --to-revision=3 -n jahez-prodtarget revision
                                      -n, --namespacekubectl rollout status deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prodnamespace of the object
                                      Examples · by task

kubectl argo rollouts undo menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
kubectl argo rollouts get rollout menu-rollout -n jahez-prod
                                      8.6 · 8. Commands

                                      Troubleshooting

                                      In one sentence

                                      Most rollout failures are one of eight errors; the number on the diagram tells you which stage raised it.

                                      #You seeStageCauseFix
                                      ①deployments.apps "menu-service" not foundAPI serverwrong name or namespacekubectl get deploy -n jahez-prod
                                      ②spec.selector: … field is immutableAPI serverselector changed in the filekubectl delete deploy/menu-service-deployment -n jahez-prod && kubectl apply -f menu-service-deployment.yaml
                                      ③surge Pod Pending · 0/3 nodes: Insufficient memoryschedulerno room for maxSurge × requestskubectl describe pod -l app=menu-service -n jahez-prod
                                      ④ImagePullBackOffkubelettag missing on ghcr.io or no pull secretkubectl describe pod -l app=menu-service -n jahez-prod | grep -A3 Failed
                                      ⑤exceeded its progress deadline · Pods 0/1 Runningkubelet · controllerreadiness never passeskubectl logs -l app=menu-service --tail=50 -n jahez-prod
                                      ⑥Rollout ✖ Degraded · AnalysisRun FailedArgo Rolloutssuccess rate below 99%kubectl get analysisruns -n jahez-prod
                                      ⑦503 NR / no healthy upstreamIstioVirtualService subset missing in DestinationRuleistioctl analyze -n jahez-prod
                                      ⑧may not be 0 when maxSurge is 0API servermaxSurge 0 and maxUnavailable 0kubectl apply -f menu-service-deployment.yaml --dry-run=server -n jahez-prod
